fixed.thermal_geometry: existing body and thermal-joint treatment unchanged

installed_source: Kevin England, personal communication via John McLennan, November 2026, from the drill pipe data sheets

premium_16B.unchanged: Body dimensions and joint OD remain the primary values; only ID and tong lengths change as declared

restriction_basis: Pin plus box tong lengths; source-length approximation, not a measured made-up constant-bore length
transition_choice: abrupt fallback: finished upset/weld/tool-joint bore profile is not established
source_choice_rule: Choose transition from applicability of sourced geometry and coefficient before scores; no pressure or slope selects it
roughness_qualification: No drill-pipe-specific value found; 45.72 micrometres is the entry 10 EPA new water-steel transfer, applied by the existing global option including insulated pipe as a sensitivity
no_local_scope: Zero connection local losses on all joint-bearing segments, including retained HWDP and EIS insulated connections; dimensions unchanged
prediction_selection: Entry 10: one lower-median-depth input window per assembly; per-window G1/G2 changes and G3/G5/G6 proxy changes. Full frozen coverage follows only after declaration.
recommendation_rule: Recommend the installed geometry for the working calculation if paired coverage and the declared model-only pressure, temperature and heat changes are reproduced within entry 10 tolerances, regardless of score direction. Recommend the abrupt fallback only as a declared unresolved-profile approximation. Scores and trip slopes do not select geometry or transition. No adoption without maintainer decision.

prior_exposure.qualification: Previously scored catalogue FH (7.5 by 3 in joints), abrupt; bore matches the subsequently sourced installed pipe; no treatment selected from these results

trip_slopes.method_source: validation/model-development/entry-9/analyse.py, slopes; same windows, flow and depth grouping, temperature treatment, mass-rate convention and reductions
outputs: modelled pressure slope in psi per 1000 ft
trip_slopes.eow19: Report separately: the added upper length is insulated pipe. Its connection geometry remains the same declared catalogue transfer as regular pipe.

predictions.baseline: Reproduce entry 9 modelled slopes and ratios.
predictions.smooth: Raise regular and insulated per-length slopes through the pipe-friction relation; it supplies no difference in connection identity.
predictions.steel: Raise the slopes above smooth through the uniform internal roughness example on both regular and insulated pipe.
predictions.gpds: Raise 16B slopes above smooth through smaller catalogue joint bores, including insulated-pipe connections.
predictions.fh: Raise 16B slopes above smooth through smaller conventional FH joint bores, including insulated-pipe connections; expect a larger increment than GPDS55.
predictions.gradual: Reduce the repeated-connection local contribution relative to smooth in regular and insulated pipe. The net sign relative to baseline includes the opposing smooth-friction change.

trip_slopes.selection: Secondary reporting only. It does not enter the unchanged acceptance rule and cannot select any variant or equipment dimension.
